device.modelDescription: Reviews a local source repository by composing three other hosted tools -- repo-scan, secret-detect and dep-audit -- inside a single tool call. The source code the review is derived from is read, passed between the three modules in-process, and discarded: it is never part of this tool's response, and this tool's output schema has no field that could carry it. Returns the findings, a per-hop billing record, and a byte-flow report showing how much data moved internally versus how much came back.

actionList.name: review
actionList.description: Reviews a local repository for hardcoded credentials and dependency-declaration hygiene, and returns a compact report. Defaults to the countinghouse repository this tool is hosted in, so it can be called with no arguments; pass `path` to review a different directory, and include/exclude globs to narrow what is read. Internally it runs three tools in sequence -- a file reader, a credential detector and a manifest auditor -- and only the aggregate survives: no file contents, no code excerpts and no full credentials are ever returned, and the response is a few kilobytes regardless of how large the repository is. The response has three parts. `findings` is the report: what was scanned, masked credential hits with file and line, and dependency counts plus unpinned and suspicious specifiers. `bill` is one metering record per internal hop, charged to whoever called this tool. `dataFlow` reports how many bytes moved between the internal tools versus how many bytes came back to you. TWO SCOPE LIMITS TO PASS ON WHEN REPORTING RESULTS: credential detection is demo-grade regex matching, not a substitute for gitleaks or trufflehog, so a clean result is not proof a repository is clean and every hit needs human confirmation; and the dependency audit never touches the network, so it reports manifest hygiene only and says nothing about known vulnerabilities.
